questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding cytochrome P450 enzymes, except:

options.text: Most psychotherapeutic drugs are inactivated by CYP 450 enzymes by oxidation
Persons with genetic polymorphisms in the CYP genes that encode inefficient versions of CYP enzymes are considered poor metabolizers
The CYP enzymes act primarily in the endoplasmic reticulum of the hepatocytes and the cells of the intestine
Viral hepatitis and cirrhosis affect the efficiency of drug metabolism by CYP enzymes
About 25% of Caucasians have low levels of CYP enzymes and are poor metabolizers

correct_answer.text: About 25% of Caucasians have low levels of CYP enzymes and are poor metabolizers

correct_answers.text: About 25% of Caucasians have low levels of CYP enzymes and are poor metabolizers

questions.explanation: About 7–10% of Caucasians have low levels of CYP enzymes and are poor metabolizers.

questions.question_text: Regarding hepatic enzymes, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Poor metabolizers are detected by their slow metabolism of debrisoquine or dextromethorphan
Slow acetylators metabolize phenelzine slowly
Slow acetylation is an autosomal-dominant trait
Direct inhibition of hepatic enzymes is usually more profound than competitive inhibition
Haloperidol inhibits the CYP 2D6 enzyme

correct_answer.text: Slow acetylation is an autosomal-dominant trait

correct_answers.text: Slow acetylation is an autosomal-dominant trait

questions.explanation: Slow acetylation is an autosomal-recessive trait. CYP 2D6, IA2, 2C, 3A3/4 are important CYP enzymes that metabolize psychotropic drugs.

questions.question_text: Expression of CYP genes may be induced by all of the following, except:

options.text: Alcohol
Barbiturates
Anticonvulsants
Smoking
Grapefruit juice

questions.explanation: Grapefruit juice appears to inhibit CYP 3A4 activity in the gut mucosa.

questions.question_text: Cimetidine:

options.text: Is an inhibitor of CYP 3A4
Increases the metabolism of valproate
May inhibit the metabolism and increase the plasma concentration of alprazolam
Decreases the plasma concentration of mirtazapine and sertraline
Increases the risk of ventricular arrhythmias when given with sertindole

correct_answer.text: Increases the risk of ventricular arrhythmias when given with sertindole

correct_answers.text: Increases the risk of ventricular arrhythmias when given with sertindole

questions.explanation: Cimetidine is an inducer of CYP 3A4; it inhibits the metabolism of valproate, carbamazepine and phenytoin; it may increase the metabolism and decrease the plasma concentration of alprazolam, which is a substrate of CYP 3A4; it increases the plasma concentration of mirtazapine, sertraline, meclobamide and tricyclics.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true of polymorphic (allelic) variation in DNA?

options.text: It may produce proteins that interact with psychotropic drugs
It may modify the likelihood of therapeutic response
It may result in development of adverse reactions
It may affect blood levels of drugs and thereby brain exposure
All of the above

questions.explanation: Polymorphic (allelic) variation in DNA may result in the production of proteins that interact with psychotropic drugs in different ways. Genetic variation in CYP-metabolizing enzymes can affect blood levels of drugs and thereby brain exposure.

questions.question_text: Pharmacogenetic studies in psychiatry have shown all of the following, except:

options.text: Mutations in the gene for CYP 2D6 may be associated with antipsychotic drug-induced tardive dyskinesia
Alleles associated with decreased expression of 5-HT transporters are associated with better response to SSRIs
Therapeutic response to clozapine may be associated with specific alleles of the 5-HT 2Areceptor
Weight gain with antipsychotic drugs is associated with an allele of the 5-HT 2Creceptor
The pathogenic mechanism of the most prominent genes in schizophrenia includes dysregulation of the NMDA glutamate receptor

correct_answer.text: Alleles associated with decreased expression of 5-HT transporters are associated with better response to SSRIs

correct_answers.text: Alleles associated with decreased expression of 5-HT transporters are associated with better response to SSRIs

questions.explanation: Alleles associated with decreased expression of 5-HT transporters are associated with poorer response to SSRIs.

questions.question_text: According to current genetic research, the key genes that regulate neuronal connectivity and synaptogenesis in schizophrenia include:

options.text: BDNF
Dysbindin
Neuregulin
DISC-1
All of the above

questions.explanation: BDNF is brain-derived neurotrophic factor, which is a known trophic factor. Dysbindin, also known as dystrobrevin-binding protein 1, is involved in the formation of synaptic structures; neuregulin is involved in neuronal migration and in the genesis of glial cells and subsequent myelination of neurons by these cells; DISC-1 (disrupted in schizophrenia 1) is a disrupted gene linked to schizophrenia that makes a protein involved in neurogenesis, neuronal migration and dendritic organization.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pharmacokinetic properties is not applicable to most psychotropic drugs?

options.text: Highly lipophilic
Largely protein bound
Small volume of distribution
Metabolized in the liver
Excreted mainly through the kidney

questions.explanation: Because most of the psychotropic drugs are lipophilic, they tend to enter fat stores, from where they are released slowly, and they tend to have a large volume of distribution.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true about lithium?

options.text: It is filtered passively in the kidney and excretion is directly related to glomerular filtration rate (GFR)
Reabsorption occurs in the distal tubule in competition with sodium
Reabsorption increases when that of sodium is increased
Furosemide and thiazide diuretics decrease serum lithium levels
Lithium clearance is decreased in pregnancy

correct_answer.text: It is filtered passively in the kidney and excretion is directly related to glomerular filtration rate (GFR)

correct_answers.text: It is filtered passively in the kidney and excretion is directly related to glomerular filtration rate (GFR)

questions.explanation: Reabsorption of lithium occurs in the proximal tubule in competition with sodium. Lithium is also reabsorbed in the loop of Henle to a lesser extent but unlike sodium it is not further reabsorbed in the distal tubule, thus its excretion is not facilitated by diuretics such as thiazides acting at the distal tubule. Because proximal absorption is competitive with sodium, reabsorption of lithium increases when that of sodium is decreased. Conditions that increase glomerular filtration rate (GFR), such as pregnancy, increase lithium clearance.

questions.question_text: All of the following are known causes of significant elevation of lithium levels, except:

options.text: Thiazide diuretics
NSAIDs
Dehydration
Sodium restriction
Theophylline

questions.explanation: Frusemide is the safest diuretic as it acts in the loop of Henle and adequately blocks lithium reabsorption, generally without increasing the level. However, in all diuretic therapy, monitoring is required as it may cause sodium depletion. Aspirin and sulindac are the safest NSAIDs in lithium therapy. Theophylline decreases lithium levels.

questions.question_text: Which of the following explains the mechanism of action of lithium?

options.text: Inositol depletion hypothesis
Inhibition of glycogen synthase kinase 3 (GSK-3)
Inhibition of protein kinase C
Modulation of G proteins
All of the above

questions.explanation: The pharmacological action of lithium is thought to be through a second messenger system such as the phosphatidylinositol system, where lithium inhibits the enzyme inositol monophosphate, modulates G proteins and, according to recent studies, regulates gene expression of growth factors and neuronal plasticity by interaction with downstream signal transduction cascades including GSK-3 and protein kinase C.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding the prescription of psychotropic medications in pregnancy, except:

options.text: One meta-analysis has shown an increased risk of oral clefts after first-trimester exposure to benzodiazepines
If an antidepressant is required, it is probably better to use long-established preparations like imipramine and amitriptyline
There is a lower rate of congenital malformation in babies exposed to lower-potency antipsychotics such as chlorpromazine

Recent epidemiological studies have suggested that while the relative risk of Ebstein's anomaly is increased at least tenfold in infants exposed to lithium in the first trimester, the absolute risk is very low
The neural tube defect associated with anticonvulsants may be associated with folate metabolism

correct_answer.text: There is a lower rate of congenital malformation in babies exposed to lower-potency antipsychotics such as chlorpromazine

correct_answers.text: There is a lower rate of congenital malformation in babies exposed to lower-potency antipsychotics such as chlorpromazine

questions.explanation: Fluoxetine is not associated with increased risk of malformations. High-potency antipsychotics such as haloperidol are not associated with an increased risk of foetal abnormalities; however, there is a higher rate of congenital malformations in babies exposed to lower-potency antipsychotics such as chlorpromazine. Absolute risk of Ebstein's anomaly in infants exposed to lithium is between 0.05 and 0.1. The neural tube defect associated with anticonvulsants may be associated with folate metabolism but the role of folate treatment in their prevention has not been established.

questions.question_text: Neonatal complications are associated with treatment of psychiatric disorders with which of the following drugs in the later stages of pregnancy?

options.text: Tricyclic antidepressants
SSRIs
Lithium
Benzodiazepines
All of the above

questions.explanation: Tricyclic antidepressants are associated with withdrawal reactions in neonates. SSRIs may be associated with complications such as jitteriness, hypoglycaemia and respiratory difficulties. Lithium causes floppy baby syndrome.

questions.question_text: All of the following are secreted in breast milk in significant amounts, except:

options.text: Benzodiazepines
Clozapine
Fluoxetine
Lithium
Valproate

questions.explanation: The amounts of valproate and carbamazepine are considered to be too low to be harmful.

questions.question_text: Regarding the pharmacological properties of sedatives and hypnotics, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Absorption of lorazepam is poor following intramuscular injections and diazepam should be preferred in intramuscular use
Benzodiazepine-sensitive GABA Areceptor subtypes are thought to be post-synaptic in location
Benzodiazepine and alcohol cross-tolerance is explained by similar action on the GABA Areceptor
Zolpidem and zaleplon selectively activate only one of the benzodiazepine-binding sites and they lack muscle-relaxant and anticonvulsant properties
All the benzodiazepines produce a moderate decrease in REM sleep and are not associated with REM rebound

correct_answer.text: Absorption of lorazepam is poor following intramuscular injections and diazepam should be preferred in intramuscular use

correct_answers.text: Absorption of lorazepam is poor following intramuscular injections and diazepam should be preferred in intramuscular use

questions.explanation: Absorption of lorazepam and midazolam are rapid following intramuscular injections and that of diazepam is poor; the former should be preferred in intramuscular use.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true of buspirone?

options.text: It is effective in the treatment of panic disorder
Anxiolytic effects develop within a few hours
It is effective in treating benzodiazepine withdrawal
It acts through benzodiazepine receptors
It does not cause sedation

questions.explanation: Buspirone is an azapirone effective in the treatment of generalized anxiety disorder but is not helpful in the treatment of panic disorder. The anxiolytic effects take several days to develop and it cannot be used to treat benzodiazepine withdrawal. It acts on 5-HT 1Areceptors.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding benzodiazepine withdrawal, except:

options.text: It generally begins within 7 days of stopping a long-acting benzodiazepine
It is characterized by heightened sensitivity to perceptual stimuli and perceptual disturbances
The symptoms generally last for 3–10 days
It is more common with short-acting drugs than with ones with a longer half-life
It can be effectively treated with flumazenil

correct_answer.text: It can be effectively treated with flumazenil

correct_answers.text: It can be effectively treated with flumazenil

questions.explanation: Flumazenil is a benzodiazepine antagonist, useful in reversing acute toxicity produced by benzodiazepines, but carries a risk of provoking acute benzodiazepine withdrawal.

questions.question_text: Regarding the action of antipsychotic drugs on dopamine D2 receptors, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: The blockade of D2 receptors in the mesolimbic pathway leads to a reduction in the positive symptoms of schizophrenia
Impairment in the reward mechanism and the development of negative symptoms are associated more with blockade of D2 receptors in the mesocortical pathway than in the mesolimbic pathway
The blockade of D2 receptors in the nigrostriatal pathway leads to extrapyramidal symptoms
The blockade of D2 receptors in the tuberoinfundibular pathway is associated with galactorrhoea and amenorrhoea
If D2 receptors in the nigrostriatal pathway are chronically blocked, this can produce tardive dyskinesia

correct_answer.text: Impairment in the reward mechanism and the development of negative symptoms are associated more with blockade of D2 receptors in the mesocortical pathway than in the mesolimbic pathway

correct_answers.text: Impairment in the reward mechanism and the development of negative symptoms are associated more with blockade of D2 receptors in the mesocortical pathway than in the mesolimbic pathway

questions.explanation: The density of D2 receptors is much lower in the cortex; the impairment in the reward mechanism and the development of negative symptoms are more associated with blockade of D2 receptors in the mesolimbic rather than the mesocortical pathway. Blockade of D2 receptors in the mesocortical pathway is also related to cognitive symptoms, negative symptoms and affective symptoms of schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Regarding serotonin dopamine antagonism, all of the following statements are correct, except:

options.text: 5-HT 1Areceptors act as an accelerator for dopamine release
5-HT 2Areceptors act as a brake on dopamine release
5-HT 2Creceptors regulate dopamine and noradrenaline release and play a role in obesity, mood and cognition
5-HT 3receptors regulate excitatory interneurons
5-HT 7receptors may be involved in circadian rhythms

questions.explanation: 5-HT 3receptors regulate inhibitory interneurons in the brain and also mediate vomiting via the vagal nerve.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding 5-HT 2A receptors?

options.text: They excite cortical pyramidal neurons
They increase glutamate release
They decrease dopamine release
They are involved in sleep and hallucinations
All of the above

questions.explanation: 5-HT 2Areceptors act as a dopamine (DA) brake. When 5-HT binds to 5-HT 2Areceptors on post-synaptic DA neurons, this inhibits DA release. When 5-HT binds to 5-HT 2Areceptors on GABA interneurons, this causes GABA release, which in turn inhibits DA release.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding 5-HT 2A antagonism?

options.text: It may improve positive symptoms
It may reduce extrapyramidal symptoms (EPS)
It may reduce negative symptoms
It may reduce hyperprolactinaemia
All of the above

questions.explanation: The 5-HT 2A'dopamine brake' action is disrupted by an antagonist (atypical antipsychotic) stimulating dopamine release in different pathways, resulting in these actions.

questions.question_text: Which drug is best described by the given pharmacological profile? A potent antagonist at both 5-HT 2receptors and dopamine D2 receptors. Also possesses alpha-1-adrenoceptor-blocking properties. Causes hyperprolactinaemia.

options.text: Risperidone
Olanzapine
Zotepine
Quetiapine
Aripiprazole

questions.explanation: Risperidone is a benzisoxazole. It has less affinity to D3 and D4 receptors, and blocks H1, alpha-1 and alpha-2 adrenoceptors but not actylcholine receptors. It may cause extrapyramidal symptoms (EPS), postural hypotension and sexual dysfunction.

questions.question_text: Which drug is best described by the given pharmacological profile? Moderate D2-receptor-antagonist activity with anticholinergic and histamine H1 receptor-blocking property. Causes strong sedative effects, weight gain and abnormal glucose tolerance.

options.text: Risperidone
Olanzapine
Zotepine
Quetiapine
Aripiprazole

questions.explanation: Olanzapine is a thienobenzodiazepine; adverse effects include oedema, hypotension, dry mouth and constipation.

questions.question_text: Which drug is best described by the given pharmacological profile? 5-H2D2 receptor antagonist also binding to 5-HT 1Areceptors and acting as a noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor. Somnolence and dizziness are common side-effects and it causes relatively little weight gain.

options.text: Quetiapine
Aripiprazole
Ziprasidone
Zotepine
Bifeprunox

questions.explanation: Ziprasidone has a tendency to increase the QT interval and is currently not licensed in the UK.

questions.question_text: Which drug is best described by the given pharmacological profile? Partial dopamine agonist that also has 5-HT 2receptor-blocking properties. It has side-effects like insomnia, nausea and vomiting. It is less likely to cause weight gain or significant extrapyramidal symptoms.

options.text: Sertindole
Paliperidone
Perospirone
Aripiprazole
Loxapine

questions.explanation: Aripiprazole is less likely to cause extrapyramidal symptoms (EPS) and increased prolactin levels; other side-effects include agitation and insomnia.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding clozapine are true, except:

options.text: It is a potent D2 receptor antagonist
It blocks all types of dopamine receptors (D1–5)
According to positron emission tomography (PET) studies, it exerts its therapeutic effect while blocking 40–60% of D2 receptors in the striatum
It has agonist activity on the acetylcholine M4 receptor, leading to hypersalivation
It reduces the risk of suicide

correct_answer.text: It is a potent D2 receptor antagonist

correct_answers.text: It is a potent D2 receptor antagonist

questions.explanation: Clozapine is a weak dopamine D2 receptor antagonist but has a high affinity for 5-HT 2receptors.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antipsychotic depot preparations has the longest duration of action?

options.text: Flupentixol decanoate
Haloperidol decanoate
Pipotiazine palmitate
Zuclopenthixol decanoate
Fluphenazine decanoate

questions.explanation: Time to peak plasma level of pipotiazine palmitate is 9–10 days and frequency of administration is every four weeks. Zuclopenthixol has a shorter duration of action.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding the pharmacological properties of psychotropic drugs are true, except:

options.text: Amisulpride is excreted unchanged by the kidney and is regarded as safe in hepatic impairment
Moclobemide is regarded as a safe choice of antidepressant in epilepsy
Citalopram and sertraline are contraindicated in renal impairment
Pimozide and thioridazine increase the QT interval
Clozapine should not be given with carbamazepine, co-trimoxazole or penicillamine, as it may cause agranulocytosis

correct_answer.text: Citalopram and sertraline are contraindicated in renal impairment

correct_answers.text: Citalopram and sertraline are contraindicated in renal impairment

questions.explanation: Citalopram and sertraline are regarded as reasonable choices in renal impairment.

questions.question_text: All of the following are important mechanisms of action of antidepressants, except:

options.text: Stimulation of inhibitory autoreceptors in the midbrain
Autoreceptors of NA and 5-HT neurons become subsensitive
Increased monoamine function leading to activation of second messengers
Synaptic plasticity and remodelling
All of the above

questions.explanation: Elaboration of neurotrophic factors is also thought to be a mechanism ofaction.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antidepressants causes significant blockade of dopamine D2 receptors?

options.text: Amoxapine
Clomipramine
Lofepramine
Maprotiline
Mianserin

questions.explanation: Amoxapine is also an inhibitor of noradrenaline uptake. It may cause EPS and hyperprolactinaemia.

questions.question_text: All of the following side-effects are paired correctly with the antidepressant drug known to cause them, except:

options.text: Mianserin–Cognitive impairment
Lofepramine–Hepatitis
Maprotiline–Higher incidence of seizures
Amitriptyline–Insomnia
Dothiepin–Sedation

questions.explanation: Amitriptyline causes sedation and drowsiness.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true of tricyclic antidepressants?

options.text: They antagonize the hypertensive effects of alpha-2 adrenoceptor agonists such as clonidine
They are not safe to combine with thiazides and ACE inhibitors
They are safe to use with amiodarone
They may decrease the action of warfarin
Plasma level can be decreased by cimetidine

correct_answer.text: They antagonize the hypertensive effects of alpha-2 adrenoceptor agonists such as clonidine

correct_answers.text: They antagonize the hypertensive effects of alpha-2 adrenoceptor agonists such as clonidine

questions.explanation: It is usually safe to combine tricyclic antidepressants with thiazides and ACE inhibitors; they are not safe to use with amiodarone; they may increase the action of warfarin; cimetidine increases the plasma levels of tricyclics.

questions.question_text: Regarding the pharmacological properties of SSRIs, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Gastrointestinal side-effects are common
Paroxetine is associated with acute dystonia in the first few days of treatment
Ejaculatory delay and anorgasmia are common side-effects
They are more cardiotoxic than tricyclic antidepressants
Serotonin toxicity can occur when they are combined with MAOIs or sumatriptan

correct_answer.text: They are more cardiotoxic than tricyclic antidepressants

correct_answers.text: They are more cardiotoxic than tricyclic antidepressants

questions.explanation: SSRIs are less cardiotoxic than tricyclics and they lack anticholinergic effects.

questions.question_text: Fluoxetine causes significant inhibition of all CYP enzymes, except:

options.text: CYP 1A2
CYP 2D6
CYP 2C9
CYP 2C19
CYP 3A/4

questions.explanation: CYP 1A2 inhibitors are fluoxamine and duloxetine; substrates include olanzapine, clozapine, haloperidol, tricyclic antidepressants and theophylline.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a reversible MAO-A inhibitor?

options.text: Phenelzine
Tranylcypromine
Amphetamine
Isocarboxazid
Moclobemide

questions.explanation: Moclobemide does not have significant interactions with foodstuffs. It is reversible with a shorter half-life.

questions.question_text: Regarding the pharmacological properties of antidepressants, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Reboxetine is a substrate of CYP 3A
Reboxetine causes urinary incontinence
Venlafaxine causes somnolence
Duloxetine is five times more potent in inhibiting the reuptake of 5-HT than that of noradrenaline
Venlafaxine produces potent blockade of 5-HT reuptake with lesser effects on noradrenaline

questions.explanation: The most common side-effects of gabapentin include somnolence, dizziness, fatigue and nystagmus.

questions.question_text: Regarding mood stabilizers, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Valproate may be more effective than lithium in mixed affective states
Lamotrigine blocks sodium channels and reduces the release of glutamate
One of the most common side-effects of gabapentin is insomnia
A combination of lamotrigine and gabapentin can cause neurotoxicity
Gabapentin is not metabolized in the kidney and is excreted entirely by the kidney

correct_answer.text: One of the most common side-effects of gabapentin is insomnia

correct_answers.text: One of the most common side-effects of gabapentin is insomnia

questions.explanation: The most common side-effects of gabapentin include somnolence, dizziness, fatigue and nystagmus.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding psychostimulants are true, except:

options.text: In adults, the agreed indication for amphetamine is narcolepsy
Methylphenidate is approved for use in attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children
Modafinil increases the release and blocks the reuptake of dopamine and noradrenaline
Modafinil is licensed for the treatment of narcolepsy
Amphetamines can cause severe hypertension when used with MAOIs

correct_answer.text: Modafinil increases the release and blocks the reuptake of dopamine and noradrenaline

correct_answers.text: Modafinil increases the release and blocks the reuptake of dopamine and noradrenaline

questions.explanation: Most of the psychostimulants increase the release and block the reuptake of dopamine and noradrenaline, but modafinil increases alertness and decreases sleepiness, apparently through non-catecholaminergic mechanisms.

questions.question_text: Regarding pharmacological treatments to help maintenance of abstinence from alcohol, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Disulfiram acts by blocking oxidation of alcohol and accumulating acetaldehyde, causing an unpleasant reaction
Disulfiram is safe to use in patients with cardiac problems
Acamprosate is believed to act by stimulating GABA inhibitory neurotransmission and decreasing the effects of glutamate
Adverse effects of acamprosate include diarrhoea
Naltrexone is believed to block the reinforcing effects of alcohol

correct_answer.text: Disulfiram is safe to use in patients with cardiac problems

correct_answers.text: Disulfiram is safe to use in patients with cardiac problems

questions.explanation: The main contraindications for disulfiram are a history of heart failure, coronary artery disease, hypertension, psychosis and pregnancy.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs is useful in planned withdrawal of opioids?

options.text: Loperamide
Metoclopramide
Non-steroidal analgesics
Lofexidine
All of the above

questions.explanation: Loperamide and metoclopramide can be useful for gastrointestinal symptoms. NSAIDs can be useful for aches and pains. The alpha-2 adrenoceptor agonist lofexidine is as effective as methadone in ameliorating the withdrawal syndrome.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding the pharmacological management of opioid withdrawal are true, except:

options.text: In short-term non-opioid treatment, an alpha-2 agonist is recommended
In short-term treatment, buprenorphine is found to produce a better outcome than clonidine
It is recommended to start methadone in a higher dose and lower it gradually, titrating against the presence of withdrawal symptoms
Methadone may be preferable in pregnancy because of greater experience with its use
Naltrexone treatment has a role in certain dependent subjects with high motivation

correct_answer.text: It is recommended to start methadone in a higher dose and lower it gradually, titrating against the presence of withdrawal symptoms

correct_answers.text: It is recommended to start methadone in a higher dose and lower it gradually, titrating against the presence of withdrawal symptoms

questions.explanation: There is a potential for methadone toxicity in patients whose tolerance is unknown or hard to assess. It is better to start with lower doses (not more than 40mg daily) and increase them over a number of weeks, titrating against the presence of withdrawal symptoms.

questions.question_text: Bupropion is found to be useful in which of the following?

options.text: Depression
Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
Cocaine detoxification
Smoking cessation
All of the above

questions.explanation: Bupropion is a unicyclic aminoketone-resembling amphetamine. Its common uses are in depression and smoking cessation and as a second-line treatment in attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Some clinicians recommend its use in cocaine detoxification.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding sibutramine are true, except:

options.text: It is a potent antidepressant
It is used as an appetite suppressant to treat obesity
It is a reuptake inhibitor of serotonin
It may cause dry mouth and constipation
It may exacerbate narrow-angle glaucoma

questions.explanation: Sibutramine is a reuptake inhibitor of serotonin, noradrenaline and, to a lesser extent, dopamine, but it lacks any clinical antidepressant effect.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding sildenafil are true, except:

options.text: It is a non-selective phosphodiesterase inhibitor
It is effective in erectile dysfunction
It may reverse SSRI-induced anorgasmia in both men and women
It is contraindicated in pulmonary artery hypertension
It is contraindicated in people taking organic nitrates in any form

correct_answer.text: It is contraindicated in pulmonary artery hypertension

correct_answers.text: It is contraindicated in pulmonary artery hypertension

questions.explanation: Sildenafil is licensed for the treatment of some kinds of pulmonary hypertension. The most important potential adverse effect associated with sildenafil is myocardial infarction.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true of yohimbine?

options.text: It is an alpha-2 adrenergic receptor antagonist
It is used to treat both idiopathic and medication-induced male sexual dysfunction
It may cause hypertension
It blocks the effects of clonidine
All of the above

questions.explanation: Sildenafil and alprostadil are generally considered more efficacious for the treatment of male sexual dysfunction.

questions.question_text: Regarding the use of antipsychotic drug treatment and behavioural and psychotic symptoms in dementia, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Haloperidol may be useful in reducing aggression
Risperidone and olanzapine were not found to be useful in reducing aggression
The evidence suggests that the increased risk of stroke is shared by all antipsychotics
Antipsychotics can precipitate an irreversible and fatal syndrome of Parkinsonism in people with Lewy body dementia
Antipsychotics may hasten cognitive decline

correct_answer.text: Risperidone and olanzapine were not found to be useful in reducing aggression

correct_answers.text: Risperidone and olanzapine were not found to be useful in reducing aggression

questions.explanation: One review of randomized controlled trials suggested that risperidone and olanzapine were effective in reducing aggression.

questions.question_text: Regarding the pharmacological properties of drugs used in the treatment of dementia, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Donepezil is a reversible long-acting selective inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase without inhibition of butyrylcholinesterase
Galantamine inhibits acetylcholinesterase with positive allosteric modification of nicotinic cholinergic receptors
Memantine is an uncompetitive open-channel NMDA receptor antagonist with low to moderate affinity
Tacrine is a cholinesterase inhibitor with a favourable side-effect profile for use with elderly people
In addition to causing an irreversible inhibition of acetylcholinesterase, rivastigmine inhibits butyrylcholinesterase

correct_answer.text: In addition to causing an irreversible inhibition of acetylcholinesterase, rivastigmine inhibits butyrylcholinesterase

correct_answers.text: In addition to causing an irreversible inhibition of acetylcholinesterase, rivastigmine inhibits butyrylcholinesterase

questions.explanation: Rivastigmine is a pseudoirreversible (it reverses itself over hours) inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase; rivastigmine inhibits butyrylcholinesterase within the glia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a disease-modifying agent in development that acts on amyloid processing in Alzheimer's disease?

options.text: Immunotherapy using ACC 001
Beta amyloid antagonists (tramiprosate)
Gamma secretase inhibitors SCH1390499
Gamma secretase modulator (flurizan)
All of the above

questions.explanation: Positive tests of amyloid vaccines in animals have led to early clinical trials. These found evidence not only of stabilization of memory in Alzheimer's patients but also, perhaps more importantly, that amyloid plaques were removed.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding dopamine receptors in the brain are true, except:

options.text: D1 and D5 stimulate adenylate cyclase to form cyclic AMP as a second messenger
D2, D3 and D4 are more common in the limbic areas than in the caudate–putamen region
The five subtypes of dopamine receptors have common amino acid sequences and are associated with the same chromosome
Antipsychotic drugs, by blocking dopamine receptors, lead initially to an increased firing rate of nigrostriatal and mesolimbic but not mesocortical dopaminergic neurons
